entertainment.title: Hear Hans Zimmer’s Sweeping Take on Rüfüs Du Sol’s Classic ‘Innerbloom’
entertainment.summary: "Innerbloom XI" is out today, Nov. 20, the 11-year anniversary of the original's release.
entertainment.body:
Rüfüs Du Sol ‘s emotional banger “Innerbloom” is well-established dance world canon, having provided the soundtrack to weddings, anniversaries, birthdays, engagements and other extra special moments since its release on Nov. 20, 2015 — eleven years ago today.

Today (Nov. 20) the already epic track becomes even more so under the watch of legend Hans Zimmer , who’s just released his take on the song in collaboration with Rüfüs du Sol and Bleeding Fingers, the scoring collective Zimmer co-founded to make music for films.

This version, “Innerbloom XI,” maintains the nine-minute length of the original, but takes the song to Zimmer’s characteristically sweeping cinematic scale, adding strings, percussion, xylophone, a choir and layers (and layers) of other instrumentation that makes the song fit squarely among Zimmer’s unparalleled Academy Award-winning body of work.

“Innerbloom XI” is accompanied by a new film from Rüfüs’s longtime creative director Katzki, made in collaboration with visual artist Thomás Blanchard that recreates the music video for the original. Watch the “Innerbloom XI” music video below.

Coming from Rüfüs’ du Sol’s second album, 2016’s Bloom , “Innerbloom” has generated 290 million official on-demand U.S. streams and a billion official on-demand global streams, according to Luminate. The song was a major highlight of the group’s recent Inhale/Exhale tour, a global two-year run that became nothing less than the biggest electronic tour of all time .

Beyond this “Innerbloom XI” project, new music from Zimmer will next be heard in the third installment of the Dune franchise, which is in theaters Dec. 18.

entertainment.body:
Blondie has delivered the latest offering from their upcoming album, High Noon , out Feb. 26.

Their latest single, “Come Back Home,” is buoyant and evocative, despite its forlorn lyrics longing for a place to settle down. Written by Jess Wolfe and Holly Laessig of Lucius, who also contribute their vocal harmonies, the track began as a personal song before finding its way to Blondie. “We had been on tour for a few years, and wrote this song; a sort of reflection of being away for too long, and the ways in which distance and the road can mess with your mind and your relationships,” said Wolfe and Laessig in a statement. Speaking about the opportunity to work with Blondie, they said: “We grew up with Debbie Harry as the ultimate female icon of punk, rock, and disco—paving a path for women in music, blending styles, and reimagining herself. We never dreamed a song of ours would become part of the Blondie story.”

entertainment.body:
Childish Gambino has joined the club. YouTube ’s Billion Views Club, that is, for his 2018 hit “This Is America.”

The official music video for the actor and rapper’s global smash is his first to pass the streaming milestone.

“This Is America’ was a politically-charged shot that rung out around the globe, a song that explores gun violence, racism and discrimination in the United States. It was, of course, powered by its confronting, one-take music video , directed by Hiro Murai and starring Gambino.

The recording debuted at No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 chart (via mcDJ/Wolf + Rothstein/RCA), bowing as the most-streamed and top-selling song of the week. It also arrived atop the U.S. Streaming Songs and Digital Song Sales charts, and topped sales and consumption charts around the globe, including Australia . Explore Childish Gambino See latest videos, charts and news

The single was the first and only Hot 100 leader for Donald Glover’s musical alter ego, who took the stage to unveil it as the musical guest on the May 5, 2018 episode of NBC’s Saturday Night Live , which he also hosted. On the red carpet of the 2018 Met Gala, Glover spoke briefly about the song and its meaning. In a comment dripping with irony, he remarked that, with “This Is America,” he simply wanted to make a song folks could play on the Fourth of July.

He elaborated in a 2023 interview for a GQ cover story, in which he said the idea for the song “started as a joke,” and that its title was “all we had” at the embryonic stage. “It started as a Drake diss, to be honest, as like a funny way of doing it. But then I was like, this s— sounds kind of hard though. So I was like, let me play with it.”

It was no joke with critics and fans. Glover and co-writer Ludwig Goransson went on to win song of the year with “America” at the 61st Annual Grammy Awards, where it became the first rap song to ever win the prestigious “Big Four” category, which recognizes songwriters. “This Is America” went on to snag a total of four Grammys, including record of the year, best music video, and snagged the MTV Video Music Award for best direction.

entertainment.title: How High Can ‘Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping’ Reach in Its Box Office Opening?
entertainment.summary: The Lionsgate franchise's sixth installment stars Joseph Zada as Haymitch Abernathy and opens on the heels of the launch for the new 'Grand Theft Auto' video game.
entertainment.body:
Logo text The odds look to be in favor of the Hunger Games franchise, as it is likely to gobble up a box office debut on the level of its impressive hits from more than a decade ago.

Lionsgate releases The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping in 3,900 North American theaters on Friday, with the studio projecting it to gross north of $80 million domestically. However, sources expect that the film will actually open much higher, likely surpassing $100 million and potentially reaching upwards of $130 million. Adapting author Suzanne Collins’ prequel novel that was published last year, director Francis Lawrence ‘s movie carries a production budget of roughly $150 million as it brings new life to the franchise that launched with the initial Jennifer Lawrence -led The Hunger Games in 2012. Related Stories Movies 'I Play Rocky' Stars Unite With Original 'Rocky' Producer for Film's 50th Anniversary Celebration Movies The Sound of Rocky: How an Anthem Was Born

In the new film, Joseph Zada plays Haymitch Abernathy, whom Woody Harrelson portrayed in the character’s later years for the first four movies. The expansive cast of Sunrise on the Reaping includes Mckenna Grace, Whitney Peak, Jesse Plemons, Ralph Fiennes, Glenn Close, Elle Fanning, Kieran Culkin, Kelvin Harrison Jr., Billy Porter, Ben Wang, Maya Hawke and Iris Apatow.

Sunrise on the Reaping takes place in Panem on the morning of the reaping for the 50th Hunger Games, 24 years before the events in The Hunger Games , the initial novel that published in 2008. The franchise’s first five movies have surpassed $3.3 billion at the worldwide box office, with the initial four films led by Lawrence as Katniss, Josh Hutcherson as Peeta and Liam Hemsworth as Gale.

With its box office opening, the latest movie is expected to mark a significant uptick over that of 2023’s The Hunger Games: The Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes . That prequel film featured Tom Blyth as the young Coriolanus Snow — the villainous character played by Fiennes in Sunrise on the Reaping — alongside Rachel Zegler and Hunter Schafer. The Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes opened to a disappointing $44 million domestically before ending its run with $166.4 million domestically and a global sum of $361.8 million.

Sunrise on the Reaping should open with a haul much closer to the debuts for the first four movies that starred Lawrence. After 2012’s initial The Hunger Games opened to $152.5 million domestically and was followed by 2013’s The Hunger Games: Catching Fire with an even stronger $158 million, the next two films started a bit softer. In 2014, The Hunger Games: Mockingjay – Part 1 launched with $121.8 million domestically, while the second film’s debut fell to $102.6 million in North America.

entertainment.title: Dude, Where Are My Billions? Ashton Kutcher Edging Closer to Super Rich Status After Anthropic IPO
entertainment.summary: The actor and famed tech investor's venture capital firm, Sound Ventures holds a roughly 0.5 percent stake in the AI giant.
entertainment.body:
Ashton Kutcher is perhaps better known for his savvy tech investments than he is for his acting these days, and that reputation will only solidify after the blockbuster IPO of AI giant Anthropic this week.

The venture capital firm Sound Ventures, which Kutcher co-founded with music talent manager Guy Oseary in 2015, was an early investor in Anthropic, and currently holds 0.5 percent of the company, according to a report in Bloomberg . Since it started investing in Anthropic in 2023, Sound Ventures has pumped $435 million into the company and on Thursday saw a more than 1,500 percent increase in its investment when Anthropic debuted with a market cap of more than $1.5 trillion. Related Stories Music Anthropic Sued for Using Elvis Presley Music to Train AI Models Movies Now It's Clear Why Amazon Didn't Want to Release 'Artificial': It's Withering AF

According to Bloomberg , Sound Ventures’ 0.5 percent in Anthropic is now worth somewhere in the region of $7 billion, though it is unclear how much the founders will each make from the IPO as the firm has partners and manages outside capital.

Suffice to say, Kutcher will be entering the realms of the super rich very soon, if he hasn’t already hit billionaire status, with some unverified reports suggesting his net worth was north of $500 million before the Anthropic’s market debut.

Outwardly, it might seem bizarre that the breakout star of nostalgia-bait sitcom That ’70s Show , the stoner classic Dude, Where’s My Car? , and artistically questionable films like Spread , My Boss’s Daughter and Just Married has achieved such massive financial success, but a closer look at Kutcher’s long history of investing reveals that the latest Anthropic windfall is just the latest in a long series of smart moves.

Through Sound Ventures, Kutcher held stakes in tech unicorns like Spotify, Uber, Bitcoin and Airbnb, and the firm was an investor in Hugging Face before it was acquired by Nvidia for $11.2 billion.

Kutcher left Sound Ventures earlier this year to launch his own VC firm, though he remains involved as a senior adviser. A few months ago he launched Decimal Capital, a new tech-focused VC firm. Decimal was co-founded with Morgan Beller, a former partner at Andreessen Horowitz and also the man who previously co-led Meta’s Libra crypto project.

Despite his investment prowess, Kutcher is still acting and most recently starred in FX’s buzzy Ryan Murphy-produced series The Beauty which debuted in January.

entertainment.body: Detroit Lions star Aidan Hutchinson is speaking out after suffering a devastating injury. The athlete, 26, took to Instagram on Thursday, November 19, to share his shock over the incident which will likely end his season prematurely. “I honestly can’t believe it. I’ve jumped hundreds of times on a football field and never in a million years did I think this would happen to me,” Hutchinson wrote as he addressed injuring himself during a sack celebration during a game in Germany on November 15. Hutchinson vowed not to let the setback get him down, adding, “But even something like this won’t hold me back.” Hutchinson was injured after sacking Patriots quarterback Drake Maye during Sunday’s game against the New England Patriots. The football player jumped into the air in celebration before landing awkwardly on his right leg. ESPN reported on Monday that Hutchinson tore his ACL. In Thursday’s social media post, the defensive end went on to add that there was no pointing dwelling on why the unexpected situation occurred. “I can ask why over and over again, but it’ll never make sense. All I can do is surrender to the path. Only God knows why and I trust in Him,” he wrote, thanking fans for their “prayers and well wishes.” Hutchinson also made it clear that he intends to bounce back, declaring, “I always come back stronger.” Seeing the funny side, he also quipped, “That’s the last time I go airborne 😁👍.” “Hold down the fort til I’m back, boys,” he added. Hutchinson’s post comes after the Lions’ head coach Dan Campbell described the loss of the star player as a “gut punch” earlier this week. “He’s such a phenomenal player, an impact player, but more importantly he’s an unbelievable teammate and he’s one of our captains,” Campbell said during an appearance on Detroit’s 97.1 The Ticket on Tuesday, November 17. “It just stinks, man. entertainment.title: Morgan Freeman Had A Short Stint On An Incredibly Popular Daytime Soap Opera
entertainment.summary: Back when he was still establishing himself as an actor, Morgan Freeman played an architect in several episodes of the long-running soap opera "Another World."
entertainment.body:
Freeman's character, architect Roy Bingham, arrived in the fictional Bay City in an episode that premiered on October 12, 1982. Sounding exactly like the Freeman that audiences know and love today but sporting a very '80s haircut, Roy was hired by Steve Frame and Quinn Harding to work at their construction company.

The confident Roy eventually married Henrietta Morgan and the two moved to Chicago. Freeman's final appearance in "Another World" came on 14, May 1984. He would achieve breakout film success three years later when he appeared in the crime thriller "Street Smart," earning an Oscar nomination for best supporting actor.

Denis Makarenko/Shutterstock Despite having appeared in "Another World," Morgan Freeman is not actually a fan of soap operas. "Never have been," he said during a 2000 interview with The Guardian , though he understands how important soaps are because of the interactions soap actors have with viewers. "You walk into a supermarket and some woman comes up to you and starts telling you what you should be doing, what decisions you should be making... 'What's the matter with you? Why don't you marry that girl!' They're living it."

Freeman has some competition for the title of the most famous "Another World" alum. Lots of other notable actors (including Kelsey Grammer, Giancarlo Esposito, Christine Baranski, Jean Smart, and Luke Perry) also had stints on the show. In 1987, a young Brad Pitt played a basketball player called Chris in three episodes of "Another World" in what was his first credited role. Freeman and Pitt both went on to win Academy Awards, making them part of a group of Oscar-winning actors who got their start on TV .

entertainment.title: Netflix Renews Japanese Crime Hit ‘Tokyo Swindlers’ for Season 2
entertainment.summary: The hit real estate crime series returns in 2027, reuniting stars Go Ayano and Etsushi Toyokawa with writer-director Hitoshi One.
entertainment.body:
Let the grand con begin… Netflix has ordered a second season of Tokyo Swindlers , the Japanese crime thriller that turned Tokyo’s high-stakes real estate market into one of the streamer’s biggest local hits of 2024.

Go Ayano and Etsushi Toyokawa will reprise their roles as Takumi Tsujimoto and Harrison Yamanaka, respectively, with Hitoshi One returning as writer and director. Kohei Ninomiya, who previously directed episodes of the Japanese newsroom drama Elpis , will also write and direct. The new season is set to debut globally in 2027. Adapted from a novel by Japanese author Ko Shinjo, the first season follows Takumi, a negotiator recruited into Harrison’s gang of real estate fraudsters. Their most ambitious scheme involves a property worth 10 billion yen (about $63 million), with the group maneuvering around developers and evading police as Takumi’s troubled past and Harrison’s ruthless methods gradually emerge.

The series topped Netflix’s weekly series chart in Japan for six consecutive weeks — a first since the rankings began — and remained in the country’s top 10 for 22 weeks overall, according to Netflix. It also appeared on the streamer’s global non-English-language series chart for five consecutive weeks and reached the top 10 in 15 countries.

The show’s success has also extended into Japanese popular culture, with dialogue and characters becoming memes on social media.

“Right after it started streaming, Netflix came to me and said, ‘Let’s do Season 2!’” One said in a statement. “I was terrified, thinking, ‘There’s no way we can top something that good…’ But as I worked on the scripts, I started to think, ‘Wait… isn’t this even better than Season 1?’ And that gradually turned into conviction.”

Shinjo hinted that the returning con artists would be pursuing another formidable target. “Human desire knows no limits,” the author said. “Searching for something beyond money alone, they will aim for an even bigger, even harder con.”

Toyokawa offered a humorously ominous assessment of his task of stepping back into Harrison’s shoes.

One by one, the Faithful fell—and a new Traitors winner was crowned.

Ironworker Shane Beatty hammered out his spot in TV history when he became the sole winner of The Traitors: New Blood, the fifth season of the U.S. series, during the emotional two-part finale on Nov. 19.

Beatty, 32, made history as the first recruited Traitor to win the U.S. series. He joined Katie Fites in the turret after she recruited him in the Nov. 12 episode, following two consecutive Traitor banishments.

Thursday night’s two-part finale began with the banishment of Jay Vinnedge and the murder of Clyde Moser —two Faithfuls who had begun voicing suspicions about Beatty and Fites.

After the remaining contestants completed their final mission, the two Traitors survived the castle’s final Round Table, which ended with Kriste Lewis ’ banishment.

Five contestants remained for the final banishment ceremony, but they all chose to continue banishing. Fites was sent out of the game, visibly shocked when Beatty turned against her. In the final vote, Victor Vollbrechthausen was banished, despite Beatty’s attempt to keep him in the game until the end.

With only three contestants left, Beatty revealed to Faithfuls Wyatt Gillespie and Abbey Benjamin that he was a Traitor before breaking down in tears.

ABC Add TVLine on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover Pharaoh hatches his darkest plot yet on Thursday's fall finale of "9-1-1: Nashville," which ends with his long-awaited reveal, as well as a dangerous new plot that will leave fans guessing through the new year.

The biblical baddie uses an Egyptian-themed iPad game to kidnap seven children — all older siblings, in accordance with the plagues — and chain them in an empty silo. At least, it starts out empty. Water begins filling the silo, and the more people who tune in to the live stream to watch the chaos unfold, the faster the water pours in. Thus begins a race against time for the police and the 113 to find and rescue the children. They're ultimately successful, but they nearly lose one child to hypothermia in the process.

Rogue discovers another torn Bible page in the empty silo, and a fresh fingerprint leads them to the church from which it was stolen. We also get a sketch of Pharaoh, courtesy of a brave young kidnapping victim whose blindfold slipped off during the ordeal. Now all Rogue has to do is interview everyone who ever attended that church. Easy peasy.

But just when we think this case is finally wrapping up, Don stops to help someone with car trouble on his way to Ryan and Sam's baby shower — and that "someone" turns out to be Pharaoh! We still don't know his name, but he's played by AJ Buckley of "SEAL Team" fame. The next thing Don knows, he's waking up in a room, tied to a chair, seated across from Rogue. The episode ends with a chilling question from Pharaoh: "Who's ready to have some fun?"

Elsewhere in the fall finale, Cammie's new boss is revealed (to the audience) to be a straight-up menace, crank calling her in the middle of the night with a fake report about an intruder in her home. (FYI, if Camryn Manheim's performance reminded you of the 1994 Kathleen Turner movie "Serial Mom," there's a reason. Just keep reading.) Ryan also tells the rest of the 113 about Sam's pregnancy and cancer, asking Don for four weeks off to be by his wife's side.

Below, "9-1-1: Nashville" showrunner Rashad Raisani discusses the reveal of the Pharaoh, including the red herring that had us fooled; what's next for Don and Rogue in 2027; which character will be relocating to Los Angeles for the next big "9-1-1" crossover , and more.

That felt like something Pharaoh would say. RASHAD RAISANI | Well, I would say it's not over yet. We don't know all the facts, but in a good mystery, I feel like you always need a few people that you could say could have done it, and I think Nick has a lot of reasons why he could be somehow connected to this. His wife died suddenly, he has the technical capability, and he matches Rogue's profile of Pharaoh in Episode 2 almost to a T. So there has been some groundwork, and who knows, there still may be some story there.

entertainment.title: The Traitors: New Blood Finale Recap: Did Katie And Shane Eke Out The Win?
entertainment.summary: Did the traitors or faithfuls come out on top in the season finale of "The Traitors: New Blood"? Read our recap for the full breakdown.
entertainment.body:
Euan Cherry/NBC (2) Add TVLine on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover Six players left. Four faithfuls and two traitors. And everything's at stake.

When the season finale of "The Traitors: New Blood" kicks off, the paranoia inside the castle is off the charts, as the team celebrates (or tries to, at least) its big win at the final challenge. But the roundtable looms and suspicion rests on Kriste. Victor's insistence of her guilt could be the very thing traitors Shane and Katie need to slip on through to the endgame, but Wyatt has another theory: that Victor is a traitor. He's wrong, of course, but Victor's reveal that he lied about having a shield doesn't help his status among his fellow faithfuls. And the fact that he lied is sending Kriste and Abbey B. into an absolute tizzy.

When the group sits at the roundtable, stress and panic is strewn all over their faces. Victor kicks things off by vocalizing his suspicions of Kriste and Katie. But when he tells the other players that he's never lied in the game, Kriste's face lights up. The woman can't wait to tear into him for his lie, and that she does. But Victor says he wasn't trying to hoodwink anyone; he was just trying to protect Shane from the traitorous Kriste.

When the time for talk is through, the vote ultimately falls on Kriste, with Abbey citing her behavior change as a key factor in her vote. Since it's the last roundtable, Kriste is not able to tell the group that she's actually a faithful. Oh, well!

Euan Cherry/NBC Alan gathers the remaining five contestants for the season's final ceremony: The Fire of Truth. As usual, the game will only end when everyone agrees to do so, or if just two players remain. The prize pot totals out at $246,300, but if either Shane or Katie makes it to the end, the spoils are theirs for the taking.

Everyone decides to banish again, suspecting (and rightfully so) that there is still a traitor (or two!) in their midst. Victor and Wyatt both vote for Katie, with the latter stating that he sees zero fear in her eyes every morning at breakfast. Oddly enough, she fills with fear once Shane tacks on another vote to her name. (Abbey follows suit.) With that, Katie is banished from the game, leaving Shane as the lone traitor left in the game.

On the second round, Victor and Shane choose to end the game, but Wyatt and Abbey vote to banish again. The second person banished in this final ceremony? Victor. But what a ride this guy has had! From #fruitgate to being banished, and then being saved by the pardon twist, the guy played hard and fast, and you've got to hand it to him. Heck of a game. But Abbey couldn't get past the shield lie, and Wyatt couldn't shake his tiniest of suspicions. (To be fair, Victor was going to lose anyway, had he been allowed to end the game with Shane still among their ranks. Womp, womp.)

“Following a medical problem whilst in Leipzig which required urgent attention at the hospital, and on the advice of my medical team and management we had to make the difficult decision to postpone the rest of the European/UK tour until further notice,” Gillan, 81, wrote in a statement shared via Instagram on Thursday.

He added, “Regrettably, these postponements will also need to extend to the South American and Mexico shows we have booked this year.”

Lewis Gilmour told the Times .

Despite their efforts, Haskin was pronounced dead shortly before 5 p.m.

The actor’s cause of death was deferred, pending further investigation, according to Los Angeles County Medical Examiner’s Office records obtained by the Times .

Meanwhile, Gilmour confirmed an investigation into Haskin’s death is underway, though he said a preliminary investigation found no suspicious circumstances.

Plus, police confirmed that Haskin had been alone in the moments before entering the water, despite reports that he had been in an altercation with another person.

“The evidence shows the man was alone and did not interact with anyone in the period immediately before the incident,” Gilmour told the Times . “Security footage corroborates that finding.”

entertainment.title: Billy Evans Will Secure His Cut of ‘You Can See Everything’ Profits After All — and Give It to Charity (Exclusive)
entertainment.summary: After relinquishing his backend, the villain of A24's smash documentary negotiated a deal and arranged for the payout to go to a children's nonprofit.
entertainment.body:
It looks like Billy Evans will get paid for the success of You Can See Everything after all. He just won’t keep the money. Evans and his representatives have negotiated for the backend share he gave up to be paid out, according to two sources not affiliated with him or his partner Elizabeth Holmes. The money will go to an unnamed children’s charity instead of to Evans, the sources said. While the exact percentage is unknown, the total payout will be a lot bigger now than it would have been even a few weeks ago. The film has grossed $89 million domestically to date, a jaw-dropping sum for a documentary. Subject payment is a key plot point in Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim’s hit about the convicted Theranos founder and her life partner Evans. The film shows Evans back in 2023 seeking money from A24 without Holmes’ knowledge, casting him in a greedy light; the filmmakers reluctantly then agree to pay him in order to secure access and make a deal. But a title card at the end says that “Billy Evans ultimately relinquished his negotiated share of the film’s profits and would not receive backend compensation.” Related Stories Movies IDA Documentary Awards Nominations: 'Concrete Land,' 'To Hold a Mountain,' 'You Can See Everything' Among Top Nominees Movies Billy Evans Fires Back at Amanda Seyfried and Nathan Fielder: "It's My Life and I Love It"

It is unclear if Evans at the time of that relinquishing secured a payout to charity with the title card omitting that point, or if Evans had fully given up on the possibility at the time and had a change of heart after the film was released and started raking in cash. Supporting the latter timing, Page Six reported on Oct. 23, a week after the movie opened, that Evans had contacted lawyers to try to restore his deal, with no word in that story that he had even succeeded in retaining counsel let alone striking a deal.

A representative for Evans did not provide comment. A spokesperson for A24 did not immediately reply to a request for comment. Documentary subjects these days often ask to be paid, and distributors sometimes agree, usually without giving up control of a film’s final cut. That is what happened here until Evans decided to relinquish what he’d negotiated.

Speaking to The Hollywood Reporter this week, Evans said he made that decision “maybe five months ago” because the filmmakers “said it would help the project”

“I am totally stubborn, but if there’s anything that I can do to help Liz regardless of the cost, I will do it,” he said. (He explained his earlier push for money this way: “I’m a single dad with two kids whose best friend’s about to be sent to prison. And at that time I didn’t have a job. I’m trying to provide for my family and I’m really scared about what’s to come.” Evans is a member of the family that owns Evans Hotels, which operates three high-end Southern California properties including The Lodge at Torrey Pines, the Bahia Resort Hotel and the Catamaran Resort Hotel.) The new deal means A24 will be cutting a profit-participation check for Evans’ role, just not to the entrepreneur himself. The move could still possibly help Evans’ image. The entrepreneur has become a pop-culture villain thanks to moments like a domineering scene in which he shows Holmes how to whisk eggs, along with diatribes at filmmakers over questions he doesn’t like.

sports.title: Ashton Jeanty's bad season running the ball overshadows his receiving production
sports.summary: Jeanty is second in the NFL in both catches and receiving yards for a running back this season.
sports.body:
First running back drafted to last running back in the yards-per-carry rankings? Bust. Case closed.

Except it’s not that simple. There’s no excusing the Raiders’ awful rushing offense and Jeanty’s role in it, but it’s also unfair to talk about Jeanty without acknowledging that he’s one of the best receivers out of the backfield in the NFL.

Jeanty has 46 catches this season, second only to Cincinnati’s Chase Brown among NFL running backs. And Jeanty has 417 receiving yards, second only to San Francisco’s Christian McCaffrey. There are a lot of running backs who get praised for what they can contribute in the passing game -- Detroit’s Jahmyr Gibbs, Atlanta’s Bijan Robinson, Pittsburgh’s Jaylen Warren -- and Jeanty has produced more in the passing game than all of them.

Jeanty’s 17 receiving first downs are tied with McCaffrey for the most of any running back in the NFL this season. Although Jeanty has only one rushing touchdown this season, he has three receiving touchdowns, tied for the second-most among NFL running backs. (Kansas City’s Kenneth Walker has four.)

On Sunday against the Seahawks, when Raiders rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza struggled in his first NFL start, Jeanty was his leading receiver, with four catches for 46 yards. With the Raiders trying to mount a comeback in the fourth quarter, it was Jeanty turning a short pass into a 38-yard gain that got the Raiders into range for the field goal that made it a one-possession game. The Raiders lost, and Jeanty deserves his share of the blame for their inability to do anything on the ground, but the loss would have been worse if not for Jeanty being available as an outlet receiver for Mendoza.

Jeanty hasn’t been the player the Raiders thought they were getting after he was college football’s leading rusher at Boise State. But his contributions to the Raiders’ offense are real, even if they’re not spectacular.

sports.title: David Montgomery credits the offensive line after his first big game as a Texan
sports.summary: Montgomery totaled 124 yards as the Texans beat the Colts, 26-3.

Montgomery had 26 carries for 107 yards, plus three catches for 17 yards, as the Texans beat the Colts, 26-3. Montgomery nearly doubled his previous season-high for yardage, and he averaged 4.1 yards per carry after having previously never averaged more than three yards per carry as a Texan.

Afterwards, Montgomery gave the credit to the offensive line, which has been subjected to quite a bit of criticism this season.

“Everybody on our offense, on the O-line , we should believe now because we can do it as long as we stick together and we stick to fundamentals,” Montgomery said, via the Houston Chronicle . “With them guys up front, they catch a lot of heat. They did a hell of a job.”

At 4-6 the Texans still have an uphill battle to make the playoffs. But they traded for Montgomery in the hopes that he could have big games late in the season while they’re fighting for a playoff berth, and on Thursday night, Montgomery and the Texans’ offensive line did that.

sports.title: Shane Steichen on Daniel Jones remaining the starter: "We'll evaluate everything"
sports.summary: Anthony Richardson could finally get a chance to show what he can do.
sports.body:
Asked by reporters after the 26-3 loss to the Texans whether Jones will remain the starter, coach Shane Steichen said, “We’ll evaluate everything.”

The No. 2 quarterback is 2023 top-five pick Anthony Richardson. On Thursday night, he got a garbage-time drive in the fourth quarter. The three-and-out, which started at the Indianapolis 39, consisted of Richardson running for two yards and throwing two incomplete passes.

It was Richardson’s second appearance of the season; in Week 8, he got a couple of mop-up drives when the Colts trailed the Jaguars, 42-7.

At some point, Richardson deserves a real chance to play. How much worse can the Colts’ offense be?

The Colts were outgained by the Texans, 354 yards to 167. They converted one of 11 third-down tries. Jones completed 12 of 27 passes, for 144 yards, no touchdowns, and an interception.

There’s a business reason that points to the Colts eventually getting Jones off the field. His contract has a $10.51 million injury guarantee for 2027. It vests in March. They’ll inevitably bench Jones to keep him from getting an injury that would keep the Colts from releasing him before the injury guarantee converts to a full guarantee.

That’s what the Giants did to Jones two years ago. He then requested, and received, his release.

The same thing could be happening, sooner rather than later, for Jones in Indianapolis. Which means that he could be available to another team.

sports.title: Jack Ham will return to Penn State radio booth following medical emergency

sports.body:
Ham, a color analyst for the Penn State Sports Network since 2000, was transported to the University of Washington Medical Center during pregame of the Nittany Lions’ Nov. 7 game. He missed Penn State’s game against Minnesota last week.

I’ve spent a lot of Saturdays in Beaver Stadium, first on the field and then up in the booth,” Ham, 77, said in his statement. “I’ll be back alongside Steve [Jones] this weekend, and there’s nowhere else I’d rather be.”

Jones treated Ham at the scene, saving his life, according to Penn State coach Matt Campbell. Ham remained in the hospital several days before returning to Pennsylvania on Saturday.

“I’m feeling good, and I owe a great deal to the people who took care of me and stood by me through all of it,” Ham said.

Ham was a six-time All-Pro with the Steelers, with whom he won four Super Bowl championships. He also made eight Pro Bowl appearances. He earned All-America honors at Penn State in 1970.

He entered the Pro Football Hall of Fame in 1988 and the College Football Hall of Fame two years later.

sports.title: Vikings explored all options before deciding to stay in Minnesota this week
sports.summary: As Sunday's Mexico City game between the Vikings and 49ers approaches, one of the big issues is the decision of the 49ers to spend the week at altitude in Colorado Springs while the Vikings opted to stay in Minnesota.
sports.body:
On that point, multiple 49ers players have claimed that the Vikings tried to secure the Air Force Academy facility at Colorado Springs, but the 49ers had beaten them to the punch.

The Vikings, we’re told, explored all options — including going to Air Force Acadamey facility and going to Mexico City early. They ultimately decided to implement a plan premised on staying in Minnesota as long as possible.

Obviously, the Vikings could have figured out something that would have allowed them to spend the week somewhere that would have allowed for full acclimation. There are other practice facilities in Colorado. And, again, early arrival in Mexico was always a possibility.

The issue has likely become a focal point of the days preceding the game because of the dramatically different approaches used by the 49ers and Rams before their Week 1 game in Australia. San Francisco went early; the Rams arrived late. And the 49ers stunned the Rams, 27-7.

In that case, it was about time and distance traveled. Here, it’s the same time zone, and the flight is roughly four hours — not much farther for the Vikings than a trip to Seattle, San Francisco, or L.A.

Teams that play in Denver don’t spend the week in Colorado. And while the altitude results in more sideline shots of players with oxygen masks during games, no one ever says, “Well, that team lost to the Broncos because they weren’t acclimated to the altitude.”

The Vikings-49ers game won’t turn on that. If the 49ers win, it will be because they were the better team during those 60 minutes of clock time. And, if the Vikings win, it won’t be because they someone cracked the code on playing at altitude.

sports.title: Puka Nacua's suspension arises from diversion program
sports.summary: The NFL's statement announcing the three-game suspension for Rams receiver Puka Nacua didn't specify the reason for it.
sports.body:
It comes from Nacua’s entry into a “diversion program,” related to the incident that triggered a civil lawsuit alleging (among other things) that he bit a woman on New Year’s Eve.

In September, we explained that Nacua had begun the steps required to complete a diversion program, which happened without Nacua entering into a formal agreement to do so. It’s one of the unique facets of California law; namely, California gives some defendants the ability to embark on the steps to comply with a diversion program without the kind of express deal that would have automatically triggered review under the Personal Conduct Policy.

The suspension of Nacua for three games, with the acknowledgment from the league that failure “to satisfy the conditions of his diversion program” will result in “additional and more substantial discipline,” means that the mere commencement of the process of compliance, even without an express agreement with prosecutors, was enough to get the process rolling.

It also led to a negotiated conclusion that entails Nacua being suspended for games he otherwise would have missed, due to his status on injured reserve. While it all looks convenient at best and fishy at worst, it represents the outcome of a bargain aimed at resolving the situation without full-blown activation of a process that would have entailed a formal hearing before Judge Sue L. Robinson, the person jointly appointed by the NFL and the NFL Players Association to hear the evidence and to issue a preliminary decision.

sports.title: Houston Texans vs. Indianapolis Colts ‘TNF’ Week 11 fan discussion
sports.summary: Look what we have here, Rumblers: It’s a primetime matchup between a pair of AFC teams. Though we’ve had a couple this season and more frequently of late, AFC vs. AFC is about as rare as a Barbary lion these days. The trouble here is that this is a terrible matchup, featuring teams that are […]
sports.body: Look what we have here, Rumblers: It’s a primetime matchup between a pair of AFC teams. Though we’ve had a couple this season and more frequently of late, AFC vs. AFC is about as rare as a Barbary lion these days. The trouble here is that this is a terrible matchup, featuring teams that are decidedly anything other than apex hunters. That the NFL can still sell this product to anyone is an incredible feat. Yet football fans continue lining up to see awful teams take on each other. It’s not that this one is without some interest, which is due to a few star players among both Houston and Indianapolis. The issue is that as Buffalo Bills fans, you’re settling in to watch the 3-6 Texans take on the 3-7 Colts. Those two teams are a combined 6-13 — which, if you’ve done the math, is less total wins than the 8-1 Bills have on the season. Neither of these teams was supposed to flop this season, though the writing was on the wall for Indianapolis. But Houston? It’s been an epic collapse for the Texans in 2026. A once-mighty defense has proven feckless far too often this season, which has some saying that head coach DeMeco Ryans could be warming the very seat he sits on in Houston. Fair or not, the NFL is a production-based industry. If you’re like me, the game will be on simply because it helps fill the room a bit this evening. You may also share my passion for the Thursday Night Football crew, and their pre-/postgame coverage. If nothing else, there’s also the chances to see the Texans in their Nike Rivals uniforms — and yes, they sure did again steal the Oilers’ vibe. Are you looking for a reason to root on one team over the other here? What you favor depends on who to cheer on to victory. A Houston win helps Buffalo’s strength of schedule/strength of victory, which matters most for NFL teams with postseason hopes on life support. Instead, you may prefer seeing the Colts win simply so it “harms” the slotting of 2027 first-round pick they sent to the New York Jets. With that, here’s your open thread for Week 11 of Thursday Night Football. Maybe this one also turns into a decent game, like a few suspect snooze-fests in primetime before it. As always, be kind to one another — and in all things… Go Bills!

A fourth-round draft choice out of Kutztown State University in Kutztown, PA, Reed was a key piece of a Buffalo team that made 10 playoff appearances, five AFC Championship Game appearances, and four Super Bowl appearances during his time with the franchise. At the time of his retirement, Reed ranked No. 3 all-time in receptions, and while he has since slipped to No. 23 all-time, it doesn’t dampen his accomplishments at all. A more pass-happy game has replaced the style of football played during Reed’s time in the league, making his numbers that much more impressive. Nothing is binding until contracts are signed. Even then, it won’t be real until construction begins.

sports.title: Kirk Cousins on possibly playing 18 games: "Just part of the deal"

During a Thursday press conference, Cousins was asked whether he has considered the possibility of playing a game on each and every weekend of the 2026 regular season.

“I thought about it,” Cousins told reporters. “I thought about it, but added to the altitude, added to the new system, added to not knowing people’s names. Just part of the deal. And, again, kind of one minute at a time, one day at a time, one practice at a time, and kind of keep blinders on, and we’ll look up, and it’ll be March.

“But until then, I think I’m just kind of, keeping it, you know, the short game, if you will, short view in front of me, just trying to stay focused there.”

It’s the right attitude. It’s the only attitude. He has gone from a situation in which he was destined to be replaced with rookie Fernando Mendoza to a team with a 7-2 record and a realistic shot not only at making it to the postseason but also of advancing through multiple rounds when it gets there.

And he’s right about the imminent arrival of March. Given the speed with which the season unfolds, it’ll be over before anyone knows it. It’s a finite window of time and, as Cousins said after Sunday’s win over the Packers, “ There’s more to the story being written .”

sports.title: Research moves closer to identifying CTE in living patients
sports.summary: The ability to detect CTE only through autopsies prevents football players from knowing whether they have it during their careers.
sports.body:
Via ESPN, a pair of studies published by The Journal of the American Medical Association show that a new blood test could detect advanced stages of CTE in a living patient.

A study from Boston University and Banner Health was based on blood drawn from a small sample of former players during their lifetimes. Autopsies performed after they died showed that they had CTE. The researchers then found a marker for CTE based on the levels of a specific type of protein in their blood.

“I’m cautiously optimistic that we can really understand this finding and move it forward in the next five years or so,” Dr. Michael Alosco, one of the authors of the study, told ESPN. Alosco described the test as a “game changer.”

“We are still in the discovery phase and it’s a small sample size,” Alosco said in a statement released regarding the study. “But if future studies validate these findings, this blood test will allow us to detect CTE with a high level of accuracy and open the doors to clinical trials and treatment.”

The ultimate goal remains developing a test that would show any degree of CTE in a living patient. It would allow football players to know whether they already have CTE, and possibly the extent of the disease.

Football players would first have to decide whether they want to know if they have CTE and, if they do, whether they will keep playing.

More broadly, football leagues at every level would have to decide whether players would be prevented from participating if they have CTE.

The development of a test to diagnose CTE could also lead to research aimed at identifying potential treatments for it.

But in terms of the fit, in terms of how he’s been here, he’s been a pleasure to coach. So we’ll just leave it at that.”

Staley said he expects there to be a resolution to Reid’s status soon.

Reid has started all nine games this season, but his playing time has dropped in recent weeks. He has 46 tackles and two tackles for loss this season.

sports.title: With Matt Gay dealing with a hip injury, the Raiders worked out three kickers

sports.title: Bears-Lions Thanksgiving audience will be huge — and it could have been even bigger
sports.summary: Last year, both of the early Thanksgiving Day games broke the prior record for NFL regular-season audience size.
sports.body:
With one small tweak to the schedule, it perhaps wouldn’t be.

In 2025, Packers-Lions attracted an incredible 47.7 million viewers. This year, the looming battle between the 7-2 Bears and 7-2 Lions should approach (if not match . . . if not beat) that number.

The problem is the second game. The 2-7 Eagles are in soft-tank mode. The 4-6 Cowboys have disintegrated into defensive disarray. While it will still attract a very large audience given the captive audience and the usual Thanksgiving routines, it likely won’t approach 50 million.

While the NFL has granted a permanent hammerlock to the Lions and Cowboys for the traditional Thanksgiving afternoon games, a simple tweak would have set the stage for Bears-Lions to break 50 million — and perhaps to threaten last year’s record.

Here’s the idea. Why not install flexibility to flip the start times of the afternoon games?

It’s no different than the usual Sunday-afternoon flex, like the one that happened this weekend when Steelers-Eagles moved from 4:25 p.m. ET to 1:00 p.m. ET and Jaguars-Giants slid to the higher-profile slot.

On Thanksgiving, the late-afternoon game always does better than the early one. In some years, the Lions game could be viewed as more attractive than the Cowboys game. This year would be one of those years.

It’s something to consider. Getting an annual Thanksgiving Day game doesn’t mean owning the window. And given the NFL’s current willingness, on and after Week 12, to flex from Sunday to Thursday or Sunday to Monday, why not reserve the right to acknowledge that, for the two afternoon games on Thanksgiving, the “best” one should be played in the higher-profile slot?

sports.summary: Josh Allen is universally regarded as an elite NFL quarterback, but that doesn’t mean he’s immune to criticism. sports.body: Josh Allen is universally regarded as an elite NFL quarterback, but that doesn’t mean he’s immune to criticism. And when Allen criticism arises, it tends to be centered around his interceptions. From his breakout 2020 campaign through 2023, Allen reached double digits in the interception category each year. After only six in 2024’s MVP season, Allen tossed 10 a season ago and already has seven in nine games in 2026. If obtaining a doctoral in football analysis was possible, I would write my dissertation on why we can’t view interceptions in a vacuum and their presence as a necessary byproduct of properly aggressive quarterback play. And a lot more things to challenge conventional wisdom about picks from a quarterback in the NFL. That is not the objective of this article. But it’s related to that. The point here is to demonstrate how Allen’s interceptions are unique. He’s become a master of the arm-punt pick, a worst-case result on a play in which a seismic chance is made in search of a hugely positive play for the offense. And the worst-case result of the arm punt is the least damaging in the grand scheme of all possible interceptions. Shoutout to WGR 550’s Jeremy White for noticing / highlighting this trend a while ago, by the way. Since 2020, Allen has lost an average of 3.76 Expected Points Added on interceptions, the third-lowest average among qualifying quarterbacks. (naturally, all interceptions create negative EPA for the offense). The two quarterbacks ahead of him — meaning less EPA lost, on average — are 2024 draftees, Caleb Williams (3.74 lost), and Bo Nix at (3.60). This season, through Week 10, Allen has lost an average of 2.78 EPA on his seven interceptions, the third-lowest among the 35 quarterbacks with at least 100 pass attempts on the season. The second-lowest currently is J.J. McCarthy at 2.50 EPA lost on interceptions. Lamar Jackson only lost 1.78 EPA on his lone interception to date this season. sports.body: The New York Jets have solicited advice from nearly everyone on planet Earth when hiring head coaches this century. That has included The 33rd Team, Charley Casserly, and do you remember that one time when Pro Football Hall of Famer Peyton Manning made a phone call to seal the deal for Adam Gase? Great times. That can’t happen in 2027. Make no mistake about it: the Jets will be looking for a new head coach in a matter of months, but in all of those other situations, they lost the battle before it ever began. Stop relying on people outside of the building. Put your big boy pants on and make a decision for yourself. Who is the right man for that job? Darren Mougey. Woody Johnson has called Mougey “The General” this offseason when referencing him to fans. He has spoken highly of him and believes the team is going in the right direction because of Mougey. Put him in the driver’s seat for this search and allow him to vet the candidates. ESPN New York’s Jake Asman called the latest Jets HC search a “sham” on the “Jets Collective” podcast. “Woody Johnson put Mike Tannenbaum, Rick Spielman, and The 33rd Team in charge of vetting candidates. Liam Coen is a UMass alum, Mike Tannenbaum went to UMass, and again, I work with Mike, so I’m comfortable saying this to his face. We’ve had many battles on the air and off the air, but if [the] Coz reporting is right that they got the intel wrong on Liam Coen, it’s another indictment of just this sham of a search process that led to Aaron Glenn.” --- J-E-T-S!
